record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: Let K be a closed set of points in C, and let F (K) denote the family of functions f of the form Xn Ak f (z) = , z − ak k=1 where Ak > 0 and ak ∈ K, k = 1, 2, . . . , n. Find a maximal domain of p-valence for the class F (K). For p = 1, this problem was completely solved by Distler [191]; however, for p > 1, we do not even have a good conjecture. (See also Goodman [342].) (A. W. Goodman)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a closed subset of the complex plane $\mathbb{C}$. Define $\mathcal{F}(K)$ to be the family of all functions of the form
$$f(z)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac{A_k}{z-a_k},$$
where $n\ge 1$ is an integer, $A_k>0$ and $a_k\in K$ for $k=1,2,\dots,n$. For a positive integer $p$, a meromorphic function $f$ defined on a domain $D\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ is said to be $p$-valent in $D$ if for every $w\in\mathbb{C}$ the equation $f(z)=w$ has at most $p$ solutions in $D$ (counting multiplicities) and for some $w$ it has exactly $p$ solutions. A domain $D\subseteq\mathbb{C}\setminus K$ is called a domain of $p$-valence for $\mathcal{F}(K)$ if every $f\in\mathcal{F}(K)$ is $p$-valent in $D$. A maximal domain of $p$-valence for $\mathcal{F}(K)$ is such a domain $D$ that is not properly contained in any other domain of $p$-valence for $\mathcal{F}(K)$.

For $p=1$ (univalence), the maximal domain of univalence of $\mathcal{F}(K)$ has been determined. The problem is the following: for an arbitrary closed set $K\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ and a given integer $p\ge 2$, determine a maximal domain of $p$-valence for the family $\mathcal{F}(K)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The univalence ($p=1$) case was settled by Distler (1964). For $p\ge 2$ the problem remains open; related work on maximal $K_n$-domains for families of rational functions exists (e.g., Mathematical Notes article), but no complete solution or even a generally accepted conjecture for $p>1$ appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Maximal K_n Domain of a Family of Rational Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies maximal domains for families of rational functions related to Goodman's problem.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has addressed maximal domains for related families of rational functions but does not resolve the general p-valence problem.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems on Univalent and Multivalent Functions, A. W. Goodman
status_evidence.snippet: Goodman lists open problems concerning p-valent functions, noting extensions from p=1 to p>=2 may be trivial, very difficult, or false.
status_evidence.claim: Goodman explicitly raised the multivalent extension as an open problem with no known good conjecture for p>1.
